faq.q: What is an AI fashion model generator?
faq.a: It shows your clothing or accessory on a generated person. You start with a flat product photo and get a worn image for the store.

faq.q: How does the worn view get made?
faq.a: Upload a flat garment photo, choose an adult look and a scene, then generate. Check the color and cut against your reference photo.
Tops, dresses, outerwear, and bags work best. A clear flat photo gives a better reference than a wrinkled one.

faq.q: Can a store publish the image?
faq.a: Yes, on a product page or a social post. Keep a plain product photo for measurements. Downloads have no watermark and are licensed for commercial use.

faq.q: Can I choose the look and the setting?
faq.a: Yes. Choose an adult look and a scene. The person is generated. Do not present the photo as a real customer or a celebrity.

faq.q: Does the image prove how clothing fits?
faq.a: No. It does not show your size, your body, or a guaranteed drape. Publish measurements and a size chart with the photo.

faq.q: Can I use it in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Add the offer in your ad editor. Do not write the image up as a photo of a real customer.

faq.q: Will garment details stay the same?
faq.a: They should follow the reference photo, but small prints and seams can shift. Compare before you publish. The guide to [model photos without a photoshoot](page:blog-model-photos-without-a-photoshoot) covers that check.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded flat heather-gray pullover hoodie as the exact garment reference. Preserve its gray color, hood, two drawstrings, kangaroo pocket, seams and relaxed cut. Show an adult man with short hair facing the camera in a tree-lined street, with his face and the entire hoodie visible. Change only the model and setting; keep the garment details consistent.
steps.sourceHint: Keep the complete hoodie, hood, drawstrings and pocket visible.
